Hi Aamir —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a short list of items we said we'd confirm for CardioSense on data handling and region behavior: 

Summary from call:
- CardioSense will process patient-identifiable data (PII/PHI) and needs EU residency for EU patients by default.
- You also want a warm failover option that doesn’t expose primary EU data to non-EU locations unless explicitly approved.
- Audit/logging requirements: full request/response audit trail retained for two years for compliance reviews.
- Retention policy: PHI retained up to 7 years for regulated records; other telemetry shorter.

Open questions (please confirm inline):
1) For backups: are nightly encrypted snapshots acceptable as the default, or do you require continuous replication with a sub-hour RPO?
2) For cross-region failover: is warm-standby (pre-warmed capacity in a second region) acceptable versus active-active? What RTO/RPO targets would be required?
3) Keys & KMS: do you require customer-managed keys (bring-your-own) with EU key residency for EU data?
4) Logs/audit storage: must logs for EU tenants remain physically in EU or is logical isolation with access controls sufficient?
5) Contracting: would you like a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) draft now or after we confirm the technical approach?

Next steps I propose:
- Monica (cc'd) to share our SOC2 summary and a short note on how we anchor audit logs per region.
- If helpful, schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your infra/security team to walk replication options.
- I’ll prepare a draft DPA and sample residency addendum for legal review.

Thanks — looking forward to your clarifications so we can size/design the right pattern.

Best,
Ben

Ben —

Appreciate the clear summary. Answers inline below. I copied our legal mailbox for the DPA question.

Open questions answers:
1) Backups: Nightly encrypted snapshots are not sufficient for our EU production workloads. We need an RPO of < 1 hour for patient-facing data. Continuous replication is preferred but we can accept near-continuous (15 min) if architecture limitations exist.
2) Failover: Warm standby in EU is preferred. Active-active across EU/US is not acceptable for EU-resident PHI unless we can guarantee processing and key residency in EU for those requests. RTO target: < 30 minutes for critical flows.
3) KMS: Yes — customer-managed keys required for PHI at rest. Keys must be created and stored in an EU KMS (we use GCP KMS).
4) Logs: Audit and access logs that contain identifiers for EU patients must be stored in EU and access-controlled to EU personnel only. Logical isolation with enforced key/access controls may suffice, but physical residency in EU is preferred.
5) Contracting: Please share a draft DPA now so our legal can start review in parallel to the technical deep-dive.

A couple of follow-up clarifications: does Redwood persist full request/response payloads in logs by default? If so, can that be disabled for EU tenants and kept only as hashed metadata? Also, what is the default snapshot frequency and can we tune it to 15 minutes?

If we can get a proposed pattern and DPA this week we'll try to get the security team time for a deep-dive early next week.

Thanks,
Aamir Khan

Hi Aamir —

Thanks for the quick replies and for outlining the constraints. Short answers here and a proposed pattern you can evaluate; happy to take the deep dive next week.

High-level technical options (recommended):
- Region anchoring: We can pin EU tenants to an EU control plane and dataplane. That ensures primary processing, persistent storage, and audit logs remain in EU locations.
- Backups & replication: We support both snapshot-based replication and near-continuous replication. Default: hourly snapshots. Tunable: we can configure snapshots down to 15 minutes or enable WAL-like replication for sub-15-minute RPOs.
- Warm standby: We can maintain pre-warmed capacity in a secondary EU zone (same cloud region or nearby EU region) so failover meets your RTO < 30 minutes objective.
- KMS/Encryption: Customer-managed keys are supported (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). Keys can be created in EU and used such that object storage and DB encryptions reference EU-resident keys; access logs for key usage are also retained in EU.
- Audit/logging: By default we keep request metadata (timestamps, user id, model id, token counts) and redact full response payloads for EU tenants unless you explicitly opt-in. Full request/response persistence can be disabled and replaced with hashed digests for correlation. Audit logs can be exported to a customer-owned EU bucket (S3/GCS with EU location) or stored in our EU log cluster with 2-year retention TTL.

Operational notes & tradeoffs:
- Sub-15-minute snapshots/continuous replication increases egress and storage costs; we can estimate based on your QPS to pick the optimal cadence.
- Warm standby has predictable monthly cost for reserved capacity but avoids cold-start RTOs.
- For emergency manual failover to non-EU, we can implement an approval workflow that keeps keys and logs gated — this is only allowed with explicit legal sign-off.

Attachments: I attached our SOC2 summary and a short one-pager on "EU tenancy & key residency" to this reply.

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben — please share DPA draft with cardiosense legal (cc'd).
2) Aamir — if you can share an approximate QPS and data volume for EU tenants we will produce a cost/RPO estimate for a 15-min replication plan.
3) Schedule 60-minute technical deep-dive for Tuesday/Wednesday next week. Monica to present replication patterns + KMS config.

Best,
